subject: Sapphire Health — post-demo technical recap & next steps
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Cole <samantha.cole@sapphirehealth.com>, Rajiv Menon <r.menon@sapphirehealth.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Sapphire Health — post-demo technical recap & next steps

Hi Samantha / Rajiv,

Thanks again for the time today — appreciate the candid conversation and the walkthrough of your inference pain points. Below is a concise recap from our call and proposed next steps so your SRE and procurement teams have what they need to evaluate a pilot.

Key pain points we heard
- 95th/99th percentile latency spikes during batches lead to intermittent SLA breaches for your triage pipelines.
- Unpredictable unit cost from on-demand scaling; desire for more deterministic monthly run-rate.
- PHI/data residency requirements — prefer VPC-bound or private deployment options.
- Need to run an ensemble of models (two retrieval-augmented encoders + a 70B generation model) at sustained throughput.

Goals you shared
- Sustained throughput target: ~500 requests/sec (avg payload ~900 tokens, 1–3 calls per session).
- Latency SLO: p95 < 300ms for the generator step (end-to-end target including retrieval).
- Pilot timeline: PoC in ~6 weeks, production readiness in 12–16 weeks, pending procurement.

High-level technical notes from our side
- Model family: compatible with Llama-2 70B / ggml-style quantized variants; we recommend starting with a q4_0 or nf4 4-bit profile for cost/latency tradeoffs.
- Topology we suggest for the pilot: Dedicated GPU pool (mix of 2x H100 for generator + 2x A100 or 4x A10s for retrieval/encoders), fronted by lightweight CPU tokenization/ingress nodes. Prefix caching for repeated prompts and KV cache sharing between generator replicas to reduce per-token compute.
- Autoscale + burst policy: reserve baseline Dedicated GPUs for steady throughput and allow controlled burst (policy-based) to handle spikes.

Attachments included for your review: sapphire_network_diagram.pdf (high-level VPC peering + egress considerations), SLA-draft-v1.docx (baseline terms and metrics).

Suggested next steps
1) Deep-dive with your SREs/Infra: propose Fri 23 Apr, 10:00am PT (let us know if that works).
2) You to share: token distribution histogram (percentiles), sample request/response sizes, and the current peak concurrency patterns.
3) We’ll produce an initial cost projection and a proposed Dedicated sizing for the PoC.

If Friday works I’ll book a technical session and loop in Mina (SE) and Evelyn (CS). Looking forward to the next conversation.

Best,

Logan Wright
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
loganw@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0134

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Cole <samantha.cole@sapphirehealth.com>, Rajiv Menon <r.menon@sapphirehealth.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sapphire Health — post-demo technical recap & next steps

Samantha / Rajiv — quick follow-up from an SE perspective with a few clarifying questions to make the deep-dive productive: 

1) Token distribution + request shape
   - Can you share a small histogram or percentiles for input token lengths (p50/p90/p95/p99)? Also any substantial variance between clinical vs admin queries.

2) Model ensemble specifics
   - Confirming: retrieval encoders are lightweight (LLM-embedding size ~1536) and the generator is a 70B autoregressive model. Will you need multi-turn KV persistence across sessions or only short-term per-request KV?

3) Networking and egress constraints
   - For private deployment we’ll need to map out VPC peering and any mandatory IP allowlists for your SIEM tools. The attached network diagram is a draft — please annotate with any private endpoints (e.g., EHR systems) we should be aware of.

4) Quantization / perf tradeoffs
   - For the initial PoC we usually recommend q4_nf4 or q4_0 for 70B to balance perf and quality. If quality regressions are unacceptable, we can run a small eval set during the PoC to tune the quant profile.

Proposed techncial agenda for the Fri session (30–45m):
- Quick run through token & traffic profile (5–10m)
- Deployment topology and network constraints (10–15m)
- Sizing & cost estimate walkthrough (10m)
- Open items & procurement asks (5–10m)

If you can drop the token percentiles and a sample 1–2 payloads ahead of time that’s ideal.

Thanks,
Mina
Principal Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.ai | +1 (650) 555-0198

From: Rajiv Menon <r.menon@sapphirehealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samantha Cole <samantha.cole@sapphirehealth.com>, procurement@sapphirehealth.com
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sapphire Health — post-demo technical recap & next steps

Thanks Logan / Mina — good summary. A few quick notes from our side: 

- We can confirm PHI constraints — solution needs to be deployed into our VPC and satisfy SOC 2 Type II plus vendor control attestations. Can you send current audit artifacts or an SOC 2 status checklist?
- Token distribution: p50 ~ 450 tokens, p90 ~ 820, p95 ~ 1,100, p99 spikes to ~2,400 (when multi-document summaries run). I’ll share a CSV with sample payloads.
- We’re most sensitive to p95 latency on the generator stage; end-to-end retrieval+gen p95 target is 350ms, generator-only p95 target is 300ms as discussed.
- Procurement asked for an initial TCO ballpark for a 6-week PoC and then monthly run-rate for the projected steady-state (500 req/s). Please include dedicated baseline cost vs autoscaled burst delta and any estimated egress/networking charges.

Fri 23 Apr 10:00am PT works for the SRE deep-dive — please send a calendar invite and dial-in details.

Rajiv
Director of ML Platform, Sapphire Health
r.menon@sapphirehealth.com | +1 (617) 555-0102

Subject: Re: Sapphire Health — post-demo technical recap & next steps

Rajiv / Samantha — thanks for the clarifications and the token percentiles — that helps a lot. Calendar invite for Fri 23 Apr 10:00am PT is on the way. Quick operational notes before the SRE call: 

- Audit artifacts: attaching the SOC 2 status checklist and a briefing page. We’ll have our compliance lead join if your SREs request an artifacts walk-through.
- Draft sizing & quick estimate: based on your p95 and token shapes, our initial recommendation for the PoC is a Dedicated pool with equivalent of 4x H100 (generator tier) + 4x A10/A100 for retrieval/encoders; combined config should reach sustained 500 req/s with p95 generator ~230–320ms depending on quant profile and caching hit rate. We’ll formalize numbers for the call and provide an itemized PoC budget (compute, networking, support).
- Network diagram is attached (see sapphire_network_diagram.pdf). Please flag any private endpoints.
- Procurement: we’ll include a short appendix with payment terms, cancellation windows, and a 30-day trial clause in the updated SLA draft.

Action items
- Sapphire: share CSV of sample payloads and any internal egress constraints.
- Redwood: finalize PoC sizing & cost worksheet and attach SOC 2 checklist + compliance briefing.

Looking forward to the call — see you Friday.

Best regards,
Logan Wright
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
